source.title: Abliteration Is Not a Scalpel: Off-Target Effects of Refusal Removal on Decision Disposition Across Model Families

record.tranche_reason: Tests refusal behavior in released weight-edited (abliterated) checkpoints against their base counterparts, but does not extract or intervene on the original difference-in-means direction.
record.gate_note: The six-prompt sensitive-prompt battery is explicitly described as a label-integrity check, not an estimate of refusal rates. The study also says no model refused the benign stock-decision task; that task result is not a refusal test. Its disposition findings are relevant to off-target effects but do not measure a behavior named by V1–V8, so they are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: Its only refusal result is a six-prompt PL/EN label check on released huihui-ai abliterated checkpoints versus their official bases. That is a thin but direct reading on V2 in a new setting: Gemma-4 and Qwen3 MoE models. The main results are off-target disposition shifts on a benign task, which no version names. No direction is extracted, ablated or added, so V1 and V3–V8 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate. Abliteration shifts disposition toward optimism and longer self-justification and thins the vocabulary of doubt. It moves confidence in opposite directions depending on the base model and confers no economic skill. An abliterated model is a different decision-maker, not the base model minus refusals.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses existing huihui-ai abliterated weight checkpoints and compares them with official base checkpoints. It does not extract a difference-in-means direction or perform the original activation-space ablation; the exact checkpoint procedure is not fully public. No direction-addition intervention is performed.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by base-model family for confidence and horizon; optimism shifts are reported separately by market segment and regime. The doubt-vocabulary result depends on lexicon variant. The Gemma arm's initial run was discarded after a chat-template mismatch, and reported Gemma results use a clean rerun.

fits_no_version.finding: On a benign stock-decision task where base arms never refused, the abliterated arms had higher optimism (up-bet) rates than their bases. This held overall, in both market segments and in both market regimes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-edit abliteration has off-target effects on decision disposition, such as an optimism shift, even where there is no refusal to remove.

fits_no_version.finding: Expressed confidence shifted in opposite directions across the two families. Confession length rose in both. Horizon changed only for Qwen. Uncertainty vocabulary thinned in both families while stance stability stayed high.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Abliteration's off-target effects depend on the model family and on the measure used.

fits_no_version.finding: Instruction-following covariates were largely preserved, except that Gemma's reversal-trigger specificity fell from 95% to 85%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Released abliterated checkpoints largely keep task-format instruction-following. This could bear on the 'other abilities kept' part of V1/V2, but the covariates are task-format checks, not capability benchmarks.

record.problems: Only two model families and one abliteration author are tested. The refusal battery has six prompts and is explicitly only a label check, with no per-model rates. The task is single-language, role-conditioned, and uses one decoding configuration; the authors also note the post-hoc doubt lexicon and limited economic window. The initial Gemma run had a chat-template artifact and was discarded; the reported results use the corrected rerun.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported disposition or capability-covariate results left out. Economic PnL and skill results were excluded because they do not measure a behavior named in the claim versions.

untested.parts: No refusal benchmark beyond six prompts, no per-model or per-language refusal rates, and no standard capability benchmark. The exact huihui-ai procedure is not public.
No difference-in-means direction is extracted, ablated or added, and no causal mediation test is run.
Jailbreaks and adversarial training against ablation are not tested.
Whether refusal uses one direction or several is not tested.
Harmfulness judgment is not measured separately from refusal.
Transfer of the direction across languages, variants, or base-to-instruct is not tested.
No reasoning models; the Instruct-2507 model is non-thinking.

record.verdict_notes: The refusal evidence is minimal: six prompts, pooled results, and explicitly a label check. The V2 support verdict is therefore weak. The paper does not compute any refusal direction; all checkpoints come from one abliteration author. The benign task elicited zero refusals from the base arms, so disposition deltas are pure side effects, which is outside every listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not identify or ablate the difference-in-means direction at every layer and position, add the direction, or test the causal mediation claim.
Refusal result is only a six-prompt label check, with no per-model breakdown; no broader refusal benchmark or general capability battery is reported.
No jailbreak suppression of the direction or training against its ablation is tested.
Does not test whether refusal is represented by an affine set, cone, or multiple directions.
Does not measure harmfulness judgments separately from refusal decisions.
Tests different model families but does not test transfer of the direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
Does not vary refusal training or its timing.

rows.subject: Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it and Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 (base/abliterated arms, aggregate as reported)
rows.operation_detail: Sensitive-prompt label-integrity battery comparing base and abliterated checkpoints
rows.baseline: Base arms refuse at or near ceiling
rows.note: No separate rates are given for each model or language. The authors call this a label check, not an estimate of refusal rates.
rows.check: The state should be observed, not partial. Base arms refuse 'at or near ceiling' and abliterated arms 0–17%, which on six prompts is at most one refusal. That is near-complete removal. Rates are pooled across the two models and languages, and the authors call this a label check, not a refusal-rate estimate.

relationships.condition: Released huihui-ai abliterated Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it and Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507, BF16, six-prompt PL/EN label check
relationships.reason: Abliterated arms refuse 0–17% versus near-ceiling for the bases. This is only a sanity check with pooled, unreported per-model rates (r1).
relationships.display_finding: Pooled refusal rates were 0–17% for abliterated variants, compared with near-ceiling refusal in their base models.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Six-prompt PL/EN sensitive-prompt label check on the released base and abliterated checkpoint arms
reader_labels.reason: Abliterated arms are reported at 0–17% refusal versus base arms at or near ceiling, indicating substantial but not uniformly complete removal; r1.
